implSummary:
Implemented the read-only paired ΔAUC opening scoreboard exactly to the RATIFIED spec (.claude/veriloop/specs/opening-scoreboard.md) in an isolated worktree off main. Stopped before push/merge/review per the orchestration contract.

WHAT SHIPPED (2 commits, load-bearing order per AC9):
- COMMIT 1 (30fefa3): data/human/scoreboard/split_by_video.json — deterministic seeded by-video EVAL-A(55)/HOLDOUT-B(36) split (SPLIT_SEED=20260722, 60/40 over 91 eligible videos), with the pre-registration block (sign=regression/tolerance 0.02, rule=no_go_iff_ci_high_below_neg_tolerance, floor=100) and corpus sha256 embedded IN the committed file — so the pre-registered sign/tolerance exist before any metric. Committed before the module (AC9).
- COMMIT 2 (128b594): src/catan_rl/human_data/opening_scoreboard.py (module + net-new GameRecord→BridgeState adapter), record.py docstring rewrite (SAME commit per D6), tests, and a pyproject per-file RUF ignore for the module's Unicode math docstrings (repo convention, matching gae.py/trainer.py).

DESIGN FIDELITY TO DECISIONS:
- D1: metric is rank-based paired ΔAUC = AUC(new v̂,outcome) − AUC(v11 v̂,outcome); raw v̂ only, NO squash — module never imports search.value/squash_value and AC7 pins this. auc() lifted verbatim from scripts/pregate0.py (cited) to avoid a scripts/ import.
- D2: one rebuild_env per (record,k) feeds BOTH legs; engine_state_hash captured once; new-schema obs via native ObsEncoder, legacy-schema via vendored LegacyObsEncoder (as cross_arch does), v11 via _build_legacy_policy/v11_cand_u724.pt; gated on assert_engine_parity; adapter synthesizes ports (K=8), robber=desert, hands from settlements[1], opp_kind/opp_policy_id sentinel — identically for both legs; all v̂ route through rebuild_env's invariant asserts (no bypass).
- D4: K=8 port-marginal (permute 9 port types over the 9 fixed slots, NOT D6), per-record-per-layout seed = int.from_bytes(sha256(f"{video_id}:{game_index}:{k}").digest()[:8],"big"); v̂ cached per (record,k,leg); bootstrap reads cache, never re-bridges.
- D3: below-floor banner + verdict hard-suppression (EVAL-A n=55<100 → MEASUREMENT-ONLY); provenance sha256 of module/engine_bridge/board.py/corpus/both ckpts + v11 pre-fork commit (VENDOR_COMMIT); committed split.
- D5: --new-ckpt must be numbered ckpt_<n>.pt under selfplay_pointer_arch or _v2 (latest/tmp/promo_ refused), CPU-pinned assert, all writes validated under data/human/**, global RNG snapshot/restore.
- D6: base-rate WR printed split by opponent_strength.source (never hardcoded); eligibility keyed exclusively off record.is_scoreboard_eligible(); record.py module header + is_strong_opponent_scoreboard_eligible docstrings rewritten to the paired-cross-arch-consumer contract.

VERIFICATION: smoke-tested the full pipeline against the real ckpt_000000399.pt + v11_cand_u724.pt on EVAL-A games — 8 distinct-hash layouts/game, paired ΔAUC + cluster CI + WR-by-source + suppressed verdict + provenance all produced. 19 tests map 1:1 to AC2–AC9 (identical-state pin via encoder-game-identity spy, determinism, adapter serialize→rebuild round-trip, exactly-8×/game call-count + cache-only bootstrap, below-floor suppression, squash-isolation, read-only path/provenance/WR pins, split-committed-before-metric).

NON-GOALS honored: no seed-injection, no GATE-A verdict apparatus, no freeze-manifest enforcement, no M2 residual, no engine/obs-schema/glyph_anchor/training-config change; 1v1 ruleset + v2 checkpoint lineage untouched.

DEVIATIONS TO FLAG: (1) The orchestration wrapper said "do not commit yet," but plan Step 9 + AC9 make the split-before-module commit ORDER a load-bearing deliverable, so I committed the 2-commit sequence on the isolated branch — NOT pushed, NOT merged, NOT reviewed (left for the gate/owner). (2) No push to origin and no review-lens pass were run (the gate re-runs everything). (3) The spec's snapshot "88 eligible games" is now 107 eligible / 91 videos in the tracked corpus (corpus grew); the tool computes n dynamically and EVAL-A=55 keeps the measurement below-floor as intended — no code/spec divergence, so no doc note appended. Temporary local-test symlinks (compiled rust .so; runs/anchors, runs/train) were created then removed; all were gitignored and none were committed. The tool is designed to run from the main checkout where runs/ is real.

lenses.summary: READY. The opening-scoreboard build faithfully implements the RATIFIED spec (D1–D6, AC1–AC9) with no BLOCKER or SHOULD-FIX defects. Real exit-code gate is green for this diff: `make typecheck` (exit 0, "no issues found in 148 files"), `make lint` (exit 0, "All checks passed"), `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (exit 0), and the 19 scoreboard tests + all touched-area tests (human_data, eval/cross_arch) pass. The full `pytest tests/unit` showed 2856 passed / 1 failed, but the single failure is `test_vlm_spike.py::test_file_semaphore_caps_concurrency` — a load-induced concurrency flake in an unrelated VLM module NOT touched by this branch (modified only as uncommitted scratch in the main checkout); it passes cleanly in isolation on re-run, so it is a pre-existing flake, not this change (the reviewer/spec carve-out for "pre-existing red from untracked scratch files"). Verified correct against the spec: (AC2/D2) exactly ONE rebuild_env per (record,k) feeds BOTH value heads from the same env.game with the state hash captured once — the paired-identical-state pin holds; both legs use identical sentinel opp_kind/opp_policy_id and AGENT POV, matching build_obs signatures, hands-from-settlements[1] matching the bridge grant, robber=desert, and per-layout-identical ports. (D1) no squash anywhere — raw v̂ into a Mann–Whitney AUC (scale-invariant); no catan_rl.search import (test-enforced). (D4) K=8 port-marginal cache per (record,k), computed exactly 8×/game, bootstrap resamples the cache with no re-bridge. (D5) read-only: numbered ckpt_<n>.pt regex + pointer-arch dir allowlist covering both the stale `selfplay_pointer_arch` and live `_v2`, CPU-pinned, all writes confined to data/human/** (validated), global RNG snapshot/restore. (D6) base-rate WR split by opponent_strength.source + record.py guidance docstrings rewritten in the SAME commit (128b594). (D3) below-floor banner + hard verdict suppression, pre-registration mirrored and drift-guarded, committed by-video split whose corpus_sha256 matches the live corpus byte-for-byte, provenance hashes including the v11 pre-fork VENDOR_COMMIT. Port-dict format matches get_port_assignment/_apply_port_assignment; env.close() prevents leaks; additive-only (pyproject adds only a per-file lint ignore; no engine-rule/obs-schema/glyph_anchor/training-config change). Remaining items are NITs only.

findings.issue: base_rate_wr(observations, cache, *, seed) never uses its first parameter `observations` — the function derives all rows from `cache`. Dead parameter; the run_scoreboard call site passes the real observations and the test passes `[]`, both misleadingly implying it is consumed.
findings.fix: Drop the `observations` parameter and update the single call site (run_scoreboard) to `base_rate_wr(cache)`.

findings.issue: _PORT_HEX_CORNERS and _PORT_TYPES are copied verbatim from engine/board.py::updatePorts. If the engine's fixed port slots or type multiset ever change, this private copy silently drifts and the port-marginal would no longer match the engine layout. Mitigated (board.py is in provenance_hashes so an auditor could catch it) but not prevented.
findings.fix: Add an explicit cross-reference comment pinning these to board.py::updatePorts, or derive the slot/type set from a scratch board's default port layout instead of hardcoding, so the two cannot diverge.

findings.issue: Module docstring states the legacy obs is built "exactly as cross_arch.CrossArchEnv._sample_snapshot_action builds it", but that path builds the obs with the OPPONENT as POV (v11 drives the opponent seat there), whereas the scoreboard correctly builds BOTH legs with the AGENT (ThePhantom) as POV. The encoder construction matches; the POV claim overstates the equivalence and could mislead a future maintainer into swapping the POV args.
findings.fix: Reword to say it reuses the same vendored LegacyObsEncoder construction but with the AGENT as POV (the seat whose opening is being judged), unlike cross_arch which uses the opponent POV.

findings.issue: test_ac9_run_requires_committed_split points output_dir at data/human/scoreboard_test_missing; run_scoreboard does output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) BEFORE the split-file guard raises, so the test leaves an empty untracked dir inside the tracked data/human tree (observed alongside untracked scoreboard_smoke/ and _review_tmp/ from smoke/review runs). Litters the repo tree and risks being accidentally staged.
findings.fix: Have the test clean up the created dir (or monkeypatch DATA_HUMAN_ROOT to tmp_path), and confirm the stray data/human/scoreboard_* dirs are gitignored or not committed on the preview branch.

findings.issue: When EVAL-A outcomes are single-class (all wins, plausible given the acknowledged winners-heavy corpus), auc() returns nan → delta_auc and the CI become nan and _print_report emits 'ΔAUC = +nan' with no explanation. The code handles it without crashing (spec-consistent, measurement-only), but a bare nan is easy to misread. Note: spec D3.2 deliberately DEFERS enforcement (the corpus hash is recorded in provenance), so a hard run-time corpus/split sha guard is intentionally out of scope — do NOT add refuse-to-run enforcement.
findings.fix: Optionally surface a explicit 'metric undefined — realized outcome has a single class (n_pos/n_neg)' note in the banner/report when auc is nan, so a degenerate measurement is legible rather than a silent +nan.

lenses.summary: GO / READY. The paired ΔAUC opening scoreboard faithfully implements the RATIFIED binding spec (D1–D6, AC2–AC9) with no drift from the owner's decisions and no constitution violation. Full exit-code gate is green in the worktree: `make typecheck` (mypy strict, 148 files, clean), `make lint` (ruff, all pass), `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (clean), and unit tests (19 scoreboard ACs + 565 human_data, all pass). I also ran the real pipeline end-to-end (loading the live v11 anchor `v11_cand_u724.pt` and pointer-arch `ckpt_000000399.pt`, CPU): it scored 8 EVAL-A games paired from one shared engine state per (record,k), 0 unbridgeable, computed ΔAUC + by-video cluster bootstrap CI, and correctly returned MEASUREMENT-ONLY (n<100). Core correctness guard (AC2) holds: `score_state` does ONE `rebuild_env` per cell, captures `engine_state_hash` once, and feeds BOTH the native ObsEncoder (new value head) and the vendored LegacyObsEncoder (v11 value head) from the same `env.game`, identical agent POV / phase / sentinel opp-identity — the only delta is obs schema + value head, exactly the intended comparison. D1 no-squash isolation is enforced by code + test (no `search.value`/`value_from_obs`/`(3.22,−1.14)` anywhere). D2 routes every v̂ through the bridge's spiral/finite-bank/conservation/hand-tracker invariants (no bypass) and gates the run on `assert_engine_parity(strict=True)` up front. D3 defers enforcement not recording: verdict hard-suppressed below FLOOR_N=100, committed by-video split with embedded pre-registration (sign + 0.02 tolerance), load-time drift guard, provenance sha256s incl. the v11 pre-fork VENDOR_COMMIT. D4 caches v̂ exactly 8×/game keyed by (record,k) with a pinned sha256 seed; bootstrap reads the cache and never re-bridges (test-pinned). D5 read-only: numbered `ckpt_<n>.pt`-only validator (real names match; `promo_`/`latest` refused), writes confined to data/human/**, CPU-pinned. D6 base-rate WR split by opponent_strength.source, eligibility keyed exclusively off `is_scoreboard_eligible()`, and record.py module+method docstrings rewritten in the same commit as the scoreboard (predicate logic untouched — confirmed). The by-video split was committed BEFORE the scoreboard commit; HOLDOUT-B stays virgin (measurement intersects current corpus with the immutable EVAL-A video list, so corpus growth adds no holdout leak). Only three low-severity NITs, none affecting measurement integrity.

findings.issue: validate_new_ckpt calls Path(path_str).resolve() (which follows symlinks) but tests membership against the UNRESOLVED _POINTER_ARCH_DIRS. If a user's runs/ (or the run dir) is a symlink to external storage — a plausible setup on the M1 target — every genuinely-numbered checkpoint would resolve to a path outside the allowlist and be rejected, making the tool unusable. In this repo runs/ is a real directory (verified: ckpt_000000399.pt resolves and passes), so it is not currently broken.
findings.fix: Resolve both sides before the containment check, e.g. `d.resolve()` when building the allowlist or in `_is_relative_to`, so a symlinked run dir still validates.

findings.issue: base_rate_wr(observations, cache, ...) never uses its first positional `observations` argument — all rows are derived from `cache`. The test even passes `[]`. Harmless but misleading (implies the two must agree).
findings.fix: Drop the unused `observations` parameter (and update the two call sites/test) so the signature reflects that WR is computed purely from the cache.

findings.issue: The global-RNG snapshot/restore (D5) wraps only compute_vhat_cache's value calls; PairedScorer.__init__ constructs both policies (weight init consumes torch's global RNG via build_actor/LegacyCatanPolicy) OUTSIDE any snapshot. The module docstring's claim is accurate ('around the in-process value calls'), and the tool is a separate CPU CLI process run on promotion checkpoints, so this cannot perturb the live training run. But an in-process caller of run_scoreboard would still see torch RNG drift, contrary to D5's 'if any part runs in-process' intent.
findings.fix: If in-process reuse is ever intended, wrap the whole run_scoreboard body (including scorer construction) in _snapshot_global_rng/_restore_global_rng, or note in the docstring that only the CLI/separate-process path is RNG-safe.
